titlePlain: ConfigMaps and Secrets: Getting Configuration Out of the
subtitle: Lesson 11 · Kubernetes Architecture & Core Objects

code:
kubectl create configmap web-app-config \
  --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=info \
  --from-literal=FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT=true

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: web-app-config
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT: "true"
caption: The same image runs unmodified in every environment — only the ConfigMap changes.

code:
kubectl create secret generic web-app-db-credentials \
  --from-literal=DB_USER=app_user \
  --from-literal=DB_PASSWORD='Tr0ub4dor&3'

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: web-app-db-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DB_USER: app_user
  DB_PASSWORD: Tr0ub4dor&3
caption: stringData lets you write plaintext in YAML; Kubernetes base64-encodes it for storage.

code:
kubectl get secret web-app-db-credentials -o yaml
# data:
#   DB_PASSWORD: VHIwdWI0ZG9yJjM=

kubectl get secret web-app-db-credentials \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.DB_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
# Tr0ub4dor&3   <-- decoded instantly, no key required
caption: Real protection comes from RBAC and encrypting etcd at rest, not the encoding.
